title: Music Composition and Audio Engineering
answer: Score generation, stem separation, drum programming, mixing and mastering, and generated foley.

children.name: Score Generation and Composition
children.blurb: Score generation and composition covers AI systems that produce musical notation, MIDI data, or full scores for one or more instruments, rather than finished audio recordings.

sections.body: Music composition and audio engineering with AI covers systems that generate musical scores, separate mixed audio into stems, program drum patterns, automate mixing and mastering, and create sound effects. In practice, these systems work on audio waveforms, MIDI data, or spectral representations. Score generation models produce note sequences or full arrangements from text prompts or melodic sketches. Stem separation tools isolate vocals, drums, bass, and other instruments from a finished recording. Drum programming and mixing tools adjust timing, levels, and effects without a human touching a fader. Foley generation creates footsteps, cloth rustles, or ambient room tone from descriptions or video context. The site currently tracks no live audio models or AI tools, so these pages describe the field rather than specific products.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven across these tasks. Stem separation is the most mature, with widely used open source models that can split a song into four or five stems with acceptable artifacts. Score generation can produce plausible short pieces but often lacks long term structure and harmonic originality. Drum programming is reliable for genre specific patterns but struggles with human feel and unusual time signatures. Automated mixing and mastering can match loudness targets and basic EQ curves, yet professional engineers still correct obvious errors in balance and stereo image. Generated foley remains limited to simple, short sounds, and complex interactions like cloth on skin or footsteps on gravel often sound synthetic. The honest limits are that none of these systems understand musical meaning, and all require human curation for finished work.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for how AI writes melodies and full arrangements should start with Score Generation and Composition, which covers note level and structural output. Stem Separation and Restoration explains how existing recordings are pulled apart and cleaned, a task that feeds remixing and archival work. Generative Rhythm and Drum Programming focuses on beat creation and pattern variation, often used with the score page for full backing tracks. Automated Mixing and Mastering moves from creation to post production, covering level balancing, EQ, compression, and loudness normalization. Generated Foley and Sound Design addresses non musical audio for film and games, which shares some generative methods with score generation but targets environmental and physical sounds. Together the pages move from writing music, to separating and restoring it, to rhythm, to final polish, and then to sound effects outside music.
